description: Security scanner detecting Python Pickle files performing suspicious actions

written.description: Scans a pickle for the dangerous imports it would execute on load, and will fetch one straight from Hugging Face, a URL or an archive rather than making you download it first.

alive.last_commit_message:
Fix substring matching in three block-list entries (#78)

Three `_unsafe_globals` entries used a bare string where every other entry uses a
set:

    "functools": "partial"
    "torch._inductor.codecache": "compile_file"
    "torch.serialization": "load"

The classification check is `g.name in unsafe_filter`. Against a set that is an
exact-membership test, but against a string it is a SUBSTRING test, so any global
whose name happens to be a substring of the entry was flagged Dangerous:
`functools.art`, `functools.a` and `torch.serialization.oa` all reported as
dangerous imports. It also silently narrowed detection in the other direction,
since a longer name containing the entry (e.g. `functools.partialmethod`) does not
match.

No real attribute of these modules is currently a substring of the block-listed
name, so the practical false-positive impact today is nil -- but picklescan runs in
the Hugging Face Hub pipeline, where an over-broad match flags real models rather
than merely emitting a noisy warning, and the behavior is fragile against any
future edit to these entries.

Wrapping the three values in sets makes them exact matches, consistent with the
rest of the block-list.

Tests added:
- test_unsafe_globals_entries_are_wildcard_or_collection asserts no entry is a bare
  string, guarding the whole class of bug rather than these three instances.
- test_unsafe_globals_exact_name_match_only asserts substrings are not flagged.
- test_unsafe_globals_still_flag_exact_names asserts the real names remain
  Dangerous, so the fix cannot weaken detection.

The first two fail before the fix and pass after; the third passes both before and
after. Full suite green (34 passed); black and flake8 clean under the pinned
versions in requirements.txt.
